Luxury is a €1.48 trillion global industry, and that explains why luxury brand management has become such an attractive field of study. However, choosing the right programme is about more than prestige. It is about finding a course that matches your career goals, budget, and exposure to the luxury sector.

This guide looks at some of the top 10 universities for luxury brand management degree. The names below are not listed for prestige alone. They are ranked based on curriculum relevance, industry access, location advantage, and how effectively they prepare you for real luxury brand careers.

How this guide identifies the top 10 universities for luxury brand management

Instead of relying on brand reputation alone, it evaluates each university across practical criteria such as curriculum relevance, industry access, location advantage, faculty expertise, and alumni outcomes.

It also considers how well each programme connects you to real luxury ecosystems through internships, brand projects, and proximity to global hubs like Paris and Milan.

The criteria that matter more than brand name alone

Universities with structured brand partnerships and practical learning opportunities provide a clearer pathway into the sector. We see whether the programme offers luxury-specific teaching, direct industry exposure and access to relevant employers.

When a specialist luxury programme beats a general business degree

Specialised luxury management programmes typically offer deeper sector insight, targeted internships, and stronger brand connections. In contrast, general business degrees with a luxury track may provide broader flexibility but less focused industry immersion. The right choice depends on how clearly defined your career goals are.

What this ranking does not try to claim

This ranking does not suggest a one-size-fits-all “best” university. The aim is to help you identify the best-fit options, not promote a single ideal choice.

1. ESSEC Business School - France

Why is it good?

It best serves students looking for an advanced fashion and luxury management program with in-depth brand knowledge.

What are the strengths of the ESSEC Business School?

  • Dedicated MSc Luxury Management program which combines three decades of experience.
  • Strong ties with LVMH and other luxury companies through its institutional partnerships.
  • Direct access to international luxury brands with its Paris location.
  • Double-degree programs through its partnerships with top educational institutions.

What should students look out for before picking ESSEC Business School?

  • High cost of living and studying in Paris.
  • Strict admissions process.

What degree does ESSEC Business School provide?

Students are awarded a Master’s in Luxury Management degree.

How to apply to ESSEC Business School?

Get more details & apply here on ESSEC.

2. SDA Bocconi - Italy

Why is it good?

The institution provides students with the option to study global luxury markets at its prestigious business program.

What are the strengths of SDA Bocconi?

  • Executive Master in Luxury Management program (EMiLUX) across multiple international cities.
  • Strong positioning in Milan which serves as a center for luxury and fashion.
  • International students get access to various luxury markets through its international modules.
  • Business-oriented curriculum which extends beyond fashion studies.

What should students look out for before picking SDA Bocconi?

  • Many courses are executive programmes.
  • Higher cost for international market access.

What degree does SDA Bocconi provide?

The university offers an Executive Master in Luxury Management.

 How to apply to SDA Bocconi

3. ESCP Business School - Europe

Why is it good?

It is ideal for students looking to study in multiple European countries and explore the European luxury market. This can also appeal to applicants researching top colleges across Europe.

What are the strengths of ESCP Business School?

  • Students get access to European cities through its multi-campus educational system.
  • It provides students access to executive members and luxury companies through its industry partnerships.
  • The university maintains its position as one of the best business schools in the world.

What should students look out for before picking ESCP Business School?

  • It requires students to complete their studies in multiple locations.
  • Higher cost because of their increased need for movement and accommodation.

What degree does ESCP Business School provide?

Students get a Master of Science degree in Luxury Management upon successful programme completion.

Top career choices in fashion, beauty and heritage brands

You should do so in case you are planning to collaborate with fashion houses, beauty brands, or heritage luxury brands. It would be a prudent move to concentrate on programmes that are based in Paris, Milan or Monaco where these industries are based.

Schools such as ESSEC, IÉSEG, and the International University of Monaco are better placed to be in the fashion, cosmetics, and high-end retail environment.

Look for programmes that offer brand projects, retail exposure and internships with luxury houses. Location matters here because many roles are filled through local networks and internships rather than open applications.

Best options for international careers and global brand exposure

If you want a global career across multiple markets, choose programmes with multi-campus exposure and international cohorts. Institutions such as ESCP and SKEMA stand out because they allow you to study in different countries and understand how luxury operates across regions.

Students would be expected to understand cross-cultural consumer behaviour, global retail strategy, and international brand positioning.

Best options for career changers and early-career applicants

If you are entering luxury without prior experience, focus on programmes that offer structured learning, internships, and accessible entry requirements. Schools like SKEMA, Emlyon, and IÉSEG are often more flexible for early-career applicants.

You should prioritise programmes that provide hands-on projects, internship support and clear career pathways, as these help you build credibility in a competitive industry.

Best options for experienced professionals and executive learners

If you already have work experience and want to move into luxury or advance within it, executive or specialised programmes like SDA Bocconi’s EMiLUX can be more suitable. These programmes focus on strategy and global exposure instead of entry level placement.

They are designed for learners who want to transition into luxury leadership roles or expand their industry network.

Career outcomes after luxury brand management programmes

Choosing a luxury brand management programme often goes beyond the degree. It is about where it can take you after graduation. The demand is spread across brand management, retail, and marketing functions. However, outcomes depend heavily on programme quality, location, and your ability to convert opportunities into roles.

Roles you can expect after graduation

Graduates typically enter roles such as brand executive, product manager, retail manager, merchandising specialist or marketing and communication professional.

The exact role depends on your specialisation, internships and prior experience rather than the degree title alone.

Hiring industries and brands in the luxury ecosystem

Luxury hiring is concentrated across sectors such as fashion, beauty, watches, jewellery, and hospitality. Major groups like LVMH and Kering dominate hiring, along with brands in cosmetics and premium retail.

From internships to full-time roles - how conversion works

Most luxury careers begin with internships rather than direct full time roles. Universities with strong industry connections often embed internships into the programme.

Converting an internship into a full-time role depends on performance, networking, and timing.

Salary expectations and long-term growth

Entry-level salaries in luxury could be moderate than in other industries, especially in Europe. But then, long-term growth can be strong as you move into brand leadership or regional roles.

Career progression hinges more highly on brand exposure and experience than immediate salary after graduation.

Cost, admissions and return on investment- what applicants often underestimate

Luxury brand strategy programmes often come with high tuition, but the real cost extends beyond luxury brand management course fees. Studying in cities like Paris, Milan or Monaco hugely increases living expenses.

Coming to admissions, they tend to be competitive as well. Many courses ask for a strong academic background as well as English proficiency. Sometimes, they may also require internships, portfolios or interviews, so reviewing common study abroad interview questions can help applicants prepare. 

Salaries at the beginning of a career are moderate, especially in EU locations. However, sustained growth can be huge if you earn access to top brands, internships and industry networks. It will be wise to assess ROI based on career access, brand exposure and long term progression, rather than short term salary alone.

How to shortlist and apply without wasting a cycle

Choosing the right programme requires a structured approach. Rather than applying broadly, concentrate on developing a tight, evidence-based shortlist that aligns with your goals, budget and career direction. Once your shortlist is ready, focus on writing a strong motivation letter for each application.

A five-step shortlist process for luxury management applicants

1. Define your goal clearly

Identify your target role, sector and preferred location.

2. Filter programmes by fit

Narrow down the list based on specialised skills, geographical location and the type of programme.

3. Check cost

Compare study and living costs for financial readiness.

4. Verify programme quality

Review internships, brand partnerships and alumni outcomes.

5. Rank your final options

Narrow down to 2-3 strong choices before applying.

Questions to ask before applying

  • Does the programme offer real luxury brand exposure?
  • Are internships integrated or self-managed?
  • What kind of roles do graduates often secure?
  • Is the location in line with your target industry?

Red flags to watch for

  • Vague placement or luxury industry internship claims
  • Weak or unclear luxury specialisation
  • Limited industry connections or brand partnerships
  • Programmes that look broad but lack focus

A focused, well-researched shortlist helps you avoid wasted applications and make stronger, more strategic choices.

Frequently Asked Questions 

Is a luxury brand management degree worth it for international students?

It can be if the course includes good industry networking opportunities. Even industry internships and exposure to luxury hubs can help. Success depends on location, network and brand access.

Which country is best for studying luxury brand management?

France and Italy stand out for their appeal. Cities like Paris and Milan offer better internship and job access. Ideally, students choose a country on the basis of their target sector and preferred work market after completing a course in luxury management in France.

Do you need work experience to enrol in a luxury brand management course?

Not always. Most MScs do not require work experience. But executive courses usually need work experience through internships or experience. It spans fields like fashion, marketing or retail.

What is the difference between luxury management and fashion management?

Luxury management covers an extensive range of sectors, including beauty, jewellery, hospitality as well as premium services. Fashion management focuses specifically on apparel and retail.

Are there undergraduate degrees in luxury brand management?

Many luxury brand management programmes are provided at the postgraduate level. Some universities offer undergraduate degrees in fashion or business with luxury elements, but specialised luxury training is typically designed for master’s-level study.

Which universities have the strongest links with luxury brands?

Institutions located in luxury hubs and those with structured partnerships tend to offer strong industry access. You may look for meaningful connections with internships, brand projects and alumni networks in luxury companies.

Can a general marketing or MBA programme help in building a luxury career?

General programmes target broader skills. Students comparing luxury routes with broader business management options in the UK may still need to gain experience in luxury through internships, projects or contacts. A luxury specific degree gives a head start.

Ending note

Finding a prestigious university doesn’t automatically mean you have found the best luxury brand management programme for you. It is imperative to look for a programme that matches your career goals, industry interests and future aspirations.

The strongest options combine relevant curriculum, real industry exposure and location advantage. Whether you choose a specialised luxury degree or a broader management route, your success will depend on how effectively you use the opportunities available during the programme.

The next step is clear: define your career direction and shortlist programmes at the top 10 universities for luxury brand management that match your goals before applying.
